To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
intraperitoneally administered FCA or Tetrahymena induce significant upregulation in channel catfish AMPP levels.

intraperitoneally injecting either Freund's complete Adjuvant (FAC) or live Tetrahymana pyriformis upregulated the expression of antibacterial activity and the major antibacterial polypeptide in channel catfish, HLP 1.

intraperitoneally injected Freund's complete ad juvant (FCA), a potent adjuvant in mammals, and the parasitic ciliate Tetrahymena, a natural pathogen in channel catfish, both induced a fivefold upregulation of antimicrobial polyp epides (AMPPs), the major innate immune effector molecule in fish.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of antimicrobial polypetides from fish skin.
the role that innate immunity plays in the protection of fish from disease and how this innate immunity can be stimulated to improve fish health.
the development and application of molecular techniques in fish immunology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AMPP up-regulation can be used as an effective strategy to enhance resistance of channel catfish to disease.
FCA immunostimulated channel catfish to express AMPPs in the skin to concentrations that were well within the range of concentrations that are inhibitory to many fish pathogens in vitro.

the expression of AMPPs in fish can be induced to levels that are inhibitory to many pathogens in vitro and that the expression of these polypeptides is upregulated in response to microbial challenge in vivo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

AMPPs are upregulated to levels that are inhibitory to many fish pathogens in vivo, that the response is transient and that the response is dependent on the nature and intensity of the immunostimulating agent.
FCA immunostimulated the expression of AMPP in channel fish skin and the upregulation was associated with a significant increase in antibacterial activity in the skin.
FCA is an excellent adjuvant for inducing upregulation of AMPP in channel fish skin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AMPPs are a major component of innate immunity in fish and can be upregulated to high levels in vivo by immunostimulation with FCA or challenge with live Tetrahymenas.
AMPPs are upregulated in vivo in channel catfish and that the upregulation may have a significant impact on the resistance of fish against disease.

AMPPs in the epidermal mucus of channel catfish are upregulated in response to immunostimulation, and that the levels expressed are well within the concentration range that is inhibitory to many fish pathogens.
